"Create a complete, playable 3D formula racing web game inspired by \"Dawn Force\" by Ira Games, featuring low-poly aesthetics and a cockpit view. The code must be self-contained in a single HTML file using HTML5 Canvas or Three.js (or vanilla WebGL/Canvas 3D projection if self-contained without heavy CDN dependencies).

Key features to include:
1. Title Screen @COMMENT_BODY@ Branding: Display \"DOWNFORCE\" with a sleek futuristic font and \"Developed by Ira Games\" branding on the main menu.
2. 3D Track @COMMENT_BODY@ Environment: A low-poly circuit inspired by coastal city tracks (such as Mumbai Marine Drive), featuring a curved road with lane markings, green-lit apex markers, roadside barriers, street lights, and distant low-poly city buildings/coastline.
3. Cockpit Perspective: A first-person driver view showing the low-poly red formula car's nose cone, steering wheel, dashboard, real-time speed counter (KM/H), gear indicator, and lap timer.
4. Racing Physics @COMMENT_BODY@ Controls: Smooth steering mechanics, acceleration, braking, and top-speed limits. Support keyboard controls (Arrow keys / WASD), touch controls on-screen for mobile devices, and gamepad/controller support (HTML5 Gamepad API).
5. Audio/SFX: Synthesized web audio engine for engine revving sounds, acceleration hums, and tire/collision screeches.
6. UI @COMMENT_BODY@ HUD: Clean arcade HUD showing current lap, best lap, current speed, gear, and mini-map or track position indicator on the side.

Provide the complete, fully functional, and runnable source code in a single HTML block.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

Hmm, safest for offline capture is to use vanilla Canvas 3D projection, no CDN. But quality with Three.js is much better. Network in capture may be available? Better to avoid CDN reliability risk. I'll build a custom 3D engine on Canvas 2D with painter's algorithm. That's entirely self-contained and can look great with low-poly style.

Actually a cockpit view + track + city + car could be done well with custom 3D. But performance and visual fidelity... Canvas 2D with thousands of triangles at 900p may be okay if we're careful (city buildings as boxes, barriers, lights, road segments as quads). We project per frame. Let's estimate: road ~120 segments * few quads, barriers ~ 240 boxes, buildings ~ 40 boxes, lights ~ 30 poles. Total ~2000-4000 polys. Canvas 2D can handle at 60fps maybe with fillPoly and no strokes. Painter sort by depth. Good.

Alternatively write minimal WebGL renderer—more performant, but more code for lighting/shaders. I could write a compact WebGL engine with per-vertex colors and simple lambert lighting, ~500 lines. That would look crisper and faster. Risk: bugs harder to debug. Canvas 2D projection is more forgiving and easier to get a stylized look. I'll go Canvas 2D with careful optimization, DPR capped at ~1.5, resolution scaling based on performance.

Game "DOWNFORCE" by Ira Games. Title screen with sleek font (system fonts: "Bahnschrift", "Eurostile", "Orbitron" fallback; no external fonts to keep self-contained. Could use @font-face? no). Use letter-spaced bold condensed sans with gradient + italic skew, plus custom canvas logo? Title screen: animated 3D attract mode background (track flyover with camera moving), DOWNFORCE title, subtitle, "PRESS ENTER / CLICK TO RACE", best lap record, controls legend, audio toggle.

Track: closed circuit, coastal loop. Define centerline via Catmull-Rom from control points, sampled into N points with cumulative length. Track width ~12m. Road surface as quads between left/right edges. Lane markings dashed center/edges. Curbs red/white at edges. Barriers. Green apex markers (glowing green pylons/arrows at apexes). Street lights along seaside. Distant city buildings with lit windows; coastline/sea plane on right side, palm-ish? low-poly.

Car physics: bicycle model-ish with speed, steering. Player position along track in world coordinates, heading. Lateral velocity/grip. Simpler arcade: speed += accel; heading += steer * speedFactor; position += forward*speed*dt. Track boundaries: detect off-track by distance from centerline; apply slowdown and rumble. Better: compute nearest centerline sample (spatially indexed by progress), lateral offset; keep progress. Lap counting when crossing start line with progress accumulation. Use nearest sample search around last index for efficiency.

- steering angle max 0.55 rad; yaw rate = speed * tan(steer * k)/wheelbase, reduce at high speed via steerMax factor.
- lateral grip/slip: position integrated along heading; off-track reduces grip/speed.
- collisions with barriers: clamp lateral position to track half width + a bit; bounce and reduce speed, screech. Since barriers are at ~halfWidth + 1.2, clamp |lat| to halfWidth + 0.8, reflect lateral velocity.
